note: GitHub release assets (llvm/llvm-project, brechtsanders/winlibs_mingw, skeeto/w64devkit) are canonical. Raw GitHub-proxy mirrors (ghproxy.com-style services that proxy an arbitrary github.com URL on request) are intentionally excluded per catalog policy: they cache on first request rather than actually mirroring, so a 200 response proves nothing about the file having been there before. Curated 'github-release' mirrors run by university networks (which rsync a fixed list of popular projects ahead of time) are a different thing and are evaluated case by case -- see the NJU entry below, and the 2026-09-17 mirror hunt in NOTES.md for what was tried on TUNA/USTC and rejected.

confirmed.name: NJU (Nanjing University) github-release mirror
covers: llvm/llvm-project (only the single newest tagged release at any time -- currently llvmorg-23.1.1)
brechtsanders/winlibs_mingw (a short rolling window of recent tags -- currently the last ~9: GCC 16.1.0 posix ucrt/msvcrt releases 1-4, and GCC 16.2.0 posix ucrt/msvcrt release 1)
confirmed.does_not_cover: skeeto/w64devkit (404 -- not mirrored here at all)
confirmed.method: Directory listing fetched live and matched to releases.json entries by exact filename (the mirror's subdirectories are named by human-readable release title, not the GitHub tag, so filename is the only reliable join key); every matched candidate is then HEAD-checked for an exact Content-Length match before being applied -- this is a rolling mirror, never applied by template alone. Requires a warm-up GET (the server 302s once to set a bot-check cookie, then serves normally) -- see extra_mirrors.py.
confirmed.confirmed_count: 4/4 llvm-23.1.1 releases.json entries (windows/amd64/msvc, linux/amd64, linux/arm64, macos/arm64); 36/36 currently-listed winlibs files across the 9 rolling-window releases
confirmed.hash_verified_sample: llvm_man_pages-23.1.1.tar.xz (357052 bytes, well under the 60MB cap) downloaded in full from this mirror and sha256-verified byte-for-byte against the GitHub Releases API digest for that exact asset (66f368b2...708427349) -- exact match. This file isn't itself a releases.json entry (only the toolchain archives are catalogued), but it's served from the identical mirror infrastructure as the four llvm-23.1.1 entries that are, so it stands in for them: their own files are all 0.5-2GB, too large to fully download per the task budget. WinLibs files (100-300MB, also over the cap) were instead verified via their `.sha256` sidecar files (tiny: 129 bytes), whose content was fetched and compared textually against the vendor checksum already recorded in each entry -- exact match, e.g. winlibs-i686-posix-dwarf-gcc-16.2.0-mingw-w64ucrt-14.0.0-r1.7z's sidecar reads the same sha256 already in releases.json.

confirmed.name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine
confirmed.covers: releases.llvm.org (LLVM majors 3.4-6, the pre-GitHub-Releases era): 142 releases.json entries checked individually
confirmed.method: One CDX API query per run (https://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx, filtered to releases.llvm.org and to toolchain-archive file extensions) gets every URL ever captured under that path with a timestamp; each releases.json entry's most recent capture is then HEAD-checked for an exact Content-Length match. Genuinely partial, exactly as expected: never applied by template, every one of the 142 was individually confirmed or rejected.
confirmed.confirmed_count: 139/142 (98%) size-matched exactly; 3/142 have no capture in the CDX index at all (real gaps, not errors -- see NOTES.md)
confirmed.hash_verified_sample: no vendor checksum exists for any releases.llvm.org entry (recorded as checksum: null, same as GCC source, per NOTES.md), so a hash comparison isn't possible for this category. Instead, LLVM-3.4-win32.exe (23304447 bytes, under the 60MB cap) was downloaded in full from its Wayback snapshot and confirmed to be a well-formed, complete, non-truncated NSIS installer executable (verified with `file`) at exactly the expected byte count -- the strongest integrity check available without a published hash.
confirmed.rate_limiting: archive.org rate-limits this network hard and unpredictably (plain HEAD requests intermittently returned connection errors with no HTTP status at all, and the CDX endpoint itself failed outright on one run) -- extra_mirrors.py retries with backoff and never caches a negative result from a failed fetch (a bug that briefly did exactly that, on both the per-entry HEAD check and the CDX fetch, was caught and fixed mid-hunt -- see NOTES.md), and time-boxes itself to ~90s of Wayback work per run so a flaky run doesn't hang. Completing all 142 checks took 9 separate runs of the idempotent script.

confirmed.name: Nix hash-addressed fallback tarball cache
confirmed.url_template: https://tarballs.nixos.org/sha256/<sha256-hex>  (http:// works; both 301 to the canonical sha512/<hex> path)
confirmed.full_or_partial: partial fallback cache -- 5 of the 13 gcc source tarballs are present (4.9.4, 5.5.0, 6.5.0, 7.5.0, 15.3.0)
confirmed.method: GCC publishes no checksum, so the lookup key came from the runtimes store's own locally-computed pins (store/sha256-local.json). tarballs.nixos.org is content-addressed -- the key IS the file's sha256 -- so a 301 is definitionally the same bytes; a bogus all-zero sha256 404s. All 84 cc/nim entries that have such a local pin were swept; 5 resolved.
confirmed.hash_verified_sample: gcc-7.5.0.tar.xz (62,783,088 B = 59.9 MiB, just under the 60 MB cap) downloaded in full over PLAIN HTTP from this host; sha256 b81946e7...89ee661, exact match against the store's pin. Deleted after.
confirmed.note: Fills exactly the hole Gentoo distfiles could not: 4.9.4/5.5.0/6.5.0/7.5.0 had been pruned from the Gentoo tree, so they had no corroborating hash at all. Nix's canonical sha512 path for each is now recorded as checksum_corroboration.

rejected.candidate: https://sourceforge.net/projects/winlibs-mingw/ (the winlibs project's own secondary distribution point, per the task brief's hint)
rejected.reason: The project page and every /files/.../download URL are behind a Cloudflare interactive bot challenge ('cf-mitigated: challenge') that a plain HTTP client cannot pass -- confirmed present via web search (the project and its files are real), but no request from this environment got past the challenge to see which physical download host serves the bytes, so this remains unconfirmed rather than added.

LOOKS confirmable and is not -- worth recording as a method note. HEAD returns 200 with the exact vendor Content-Length over both https and plain http, and a bogus path in the same directory 404s, so a HEAD-only check would have wrongly confirmed it. A real GET 302s to /testpow/?url=... , an nginx proof-of-work bot challenge that no plain HTTP client passes. Not added. (Same for the directory listings, which do enumerate llvm/llvm-project correctly.)

The only host found anywhere that lists BOTH llvm/llvm-project and brechtsanders/winlibs_mingw (the last ~9 WinLibs tags, GCC 16.1.0/16.2.0), but every file request -- HEAD included -- 302s to the same /testpow/ proof-of-work challenge. 0 of 58 candidates retrievable. Blocked, not proven absent; worth retrying from a client that can solve the challenge.

Soft-200 catch-all: the directory 200s, but so does a bogus release directory AND a bogus file name, and a HEAD on a real .tar.xz returns Content-Type: text/html (the Angular portal shell) rather than the archive. Same verdict as the /nim/ path in round 2.
